newsitem.title: USA: Virgin Mary wall hanging cries red tears in Kansas.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Mary wall hanging cries red tears in Kansas.

text.p: A small, plaster wall hanging from Mexico with a painted image of the Virgin Mary has shed what seemed to be blood-like tears, witnesses said on Wednesday.

The six inch-high (15 cms) oval plaque has attracted widespread attention from Catholics and non-Catholics alike to this hamlet of 450 people in south-central Kansas since the icon began "crying" on Dec. 12, the date of Mexico's Feast of Guadalupe honouring a legendary appearance of the Virgin Mary in Mexico in 1531.
Father William Vogel of the St. Nicholas church in nearby Kinsley, Kansas, said he had seen the icon cry, but could not explain it.
"There is no doubt that there were tears, and it certainly looked like blood coming from the eyes. I don't know how to explain it in any natural way," Vogel said.
The plaque was a Christmas gift last year to the immigrant family of Thomas Holguine by his wife's sister, who bought it in Mexico six years ago.

"It's an amazing thing," Cathy Woolward, a local newspaper publisher who held the tearful icon, said. Witnesses reported seeing bloody tears well up in the lifelike eyes of the figure, then cascade down the cheeks and drip off the chin.
Diocese leaders in Dodge City -- who could declare a miracle -- were likely to be sceptical and would wait a while before investigating, Vogel said.
